page.layout: One printed page. Top: page number left, running head centred, then a full-width heading. Below: a woodcut engraving occupying the middle. Under the engraving: a verse of four lines, indented alternately, in italic. Right margin at bottom: a short catchword-like note.

l.i: Qui sua prudenti committit munia seruo,
De euentu vnquam non ambiget ille bono.
Sed quisquis stolido magno discrimine: certus
De euentu optato non erit iste diu.

page.notes: The woodcut shows an emblem: a man in a cloak with a long feather-topped staff stands between two ass-headed figures, with a burning tower and demons in clouds above. No printed text inside the engraving. The running head and heading are set in spaced capitals and italic; "EMBLEMA" is the running title. The bottom-right "Similis" is an italic side note, placed as a marginal catchword-like remark. Verse lines are reproduced as printed, including the long s rendered as s; the first verse line's "munia" and "seruo" are clear. Some letters in the italic verse (e.g. "ambiget") may be uncertain.
